**My reasoning:**

My family has been farming this land in Quzhou for generations. I have about 7 mu of flat field, which my father passed to me. I never went to school — I learned farming by watching and doing. I don't read agricultural bulletins or talk to extension workers much. What I know is what works here: wheat in winter, corn in summer. Every family in my village does this. The soil is good enough, the water table is reachable with our pump, and both crops have a ready buyer at the grain depot in town.

I will plant winter wheat on all 7 mu starting in October. I buy "Kenong 199" seeds from the supply shop in town — the shopkeeper says it resists lodging and yields well, and I've used it for three years now. For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer before ploughing and apply urea twice more — once before the ground freezes, once when the plants green up in spring. I irrigate three times: before winter sets in, again in spring when growth resumes, and once at heading. I spray herbicide early, and spray again later for rust and powdery mildew — I lost a quarter of my crop to rust five years ago and I won't let that happen again.

As soon as wheat comes off in June, I plant summer maize on the same 7 mu — hybrid seeds, no waiting. I don't plough, I just use the seeder directly into the stubble. Rain usually covers most of what the maize needs, but I'll run the pump once if July turns dry. I apply urea in two splits. I spray herbicide once right after emergence. 

I don't grow vegetables commercially — my wife tends a small kitchen plot near the house, but that's for eating, not selling.
